newsitem.title: USA: Third former soldier in N.C. race killings sentenced.
newsitem.headline: Third former soldier in N.C. race killings sentenced.

text.p: A white former Army paratrooper who testified against two colleagues found guilty of murdering a black couple was spared further time in jail on Tuesday for his role in the racially motivated slayings.

Superior Court Judge Coy Brewer gave Randy Meadows, 23, who is white, credit for 17 months he had already spent behind bars, probation for 36 months and a 50- to 78-month suspended sentence in the shooting deaths of Jackie Burden and Michael James on Dec. 7, 1995.

A jury on Monday had sentenced Malcolm Wright, another white former paratrooper, to two life terms without parole for the killings, believed to be part of an initiation ritual for a white supremacist group at Fort Bragg, North Carolina.

Meadows, of Mulkeytown, Illinois, testified against Wright. He also testified against James Burmeister, believed to be the triggerman in the shootings, who was convicted of first-degree murder earlier this year and sentenced to life in prison after a jury deadlocked 11-1 in favour of executing him.

Meadows pleaded guilty to two counts of being an accessory before the assault and one count of conspiracy to commit assault. Two charges of conspiracy to commit first degree murder were dropped in exchange for his testimony, said prosecutor Edward Grannis, the District Attorney for Cumberland County.
Grannis praised Meadows and said he was to be processed out of prison on Tuesday.
Meadows, who appeared in a blue-and-purple shirt and black jeans rather than the orange prison jumpsuit he wore to testify, told the victims' families he was sorry.
"I'm sincerely sorry. If I could change what happened I would, but I've done the best I can do to make things right," he said.
Prosecutors said Meadows was the driver the night of the killings, while Wright accompanied Burmeister as he gunned the young couple down on a Fayetteville, North Carolina, street.
Paul Herzog, who was Wright's attorney, said he was appalled that Meadows would spend no more time behind bars.
"Randy Meadows is a racist. He did everything but shave his head. None of these crimes could have happened without his participation," he said.
